chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Jarrah al-Madaini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "Let not a man drink while he is standing."

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: The man (referring to the subject of the ruling)
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah (Prophet Muhammad SAWW)
key_terms.يَشْرَبِ: To drink (imperative form indicating the action)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on drinking while standing?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Tusi in Tahdhib al-Ahkam, establishes the standing posture for drinking as a recommended etiquette (adab) rather than a strict prohibition, reflecting the Sunnah of tranquility. It is often interpreted in Shia jurisprudence as a means to ensure proper digestion and to avoid the haste associated with arrogance, aligning with the Prophetic tradition of mindful consumption.
